hypothesis: A probe/diagnose/repair offline loop over World0 (synthetic task contexts -> projection eval -> relation repair) improves projection quality without RL.
motivation: MemDream reports pre-failure graph repair via dream cycles (unverified detail).

hypothesis: A write-validation gate on LLM-authored concept cards/relations reduces semantic drift versus ungated writes.
motivation: SSGM frames consolidation as validation to prevent logical drift.

hypothesis: Projection/retrieval outcomes are a usable feedback signal for updating relation weights.
motivation: REALM and OaK both refine structure from feedback signals.

hypothesis: Rehearsal (a read refreshes the recency of what it shows), borrowed from retrieval-driven reconsolidation, would recover a meaningful share of the true endpoints World0 forgets on bigworld.
motivation: Retrieval-Driven Memory Reconsolidation rewrites memories when they are retrieved; rehearsal is the form that fits World0.
evidence: E-004: 65 of 101 forgotten endpoints were never shown; at most about 1 in 10 recoverable

history.note: E-004: the gap is one-off statements never shown, not shown items forgotten; effect on the bigworld composite ≤ 0.01.

hypothesis: Suppressing co-occurrence (generic) edges in activation improves projection quality by raising focus precision (0.60) without losing recall or closure.
motivation: Co-occurrence edges might carry activation too far from the task's context.
evidence: E-005: weight 0 raises precision +0.036 but costs −0.032 closure and −0.009 recall

history.note: E-005: a trade-off, not an improvement; parameters unchanged.
